definitions.explanation: The state of being liquid, or describing something that is in liquid form. Used in scientific, industrial, and everyday contexts.

examples.japanese: {液状|えきじょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{洗剤|せんざい}→洗剤：03304_senzai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
⟦{地震|じしん}→地震：01608_jishin⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{地盤|じばん}→地盤：04035_jiban⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{液状|えきじょう}{化|か}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The ground liquefied due to the earthquake.

examples.japanese: ⟦バター→バター：04671_bataa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{溶|と}けて→溶ける：02302_tokeru⟧{液状|えきじょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{加熱|かねつ}する→加熱する：19637_kanetsusuru⟧。
examples.english: Heat the butter until it melts and becomes liquid.

notes: Composed of ⟦{液|えき}→液：02270_eki⟧ (liquid, fluid) + ⟦{状|じょう}→状：09878_jou⟧ (state, form). Functions as both a noun and a modifier with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧. The derived term {液状化|えきじょうか} (liquefaction) is a critical concept in earthquake science — when ground shaking causes saturated soil to behave like liquid, damaging buildings and infrastructure. This was notably observed during the 2011 {東日本大震災|ひがしにほんだいしんさい} and the 2024 {能登半島地震|のとはんとうじしん}. Common collocations: {液状|えきじょう}{化|か} (liquefaction), {液状|えきじょう}{化|か}⟦{現象|げんしょう}→現象：02718_genshou⟧ (liquefaction phenomenon), {液状|えきじょう}のり (liquid glue). Part of the {〜状|じょう} (in the form/state of ~) word family: ⟦{粉状|ふんじょう}→粉状：25189_funjou⟧ (powdered), {固形状|こけいじょう} (solid).
